title: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states 'completely solves the alignment challenge between texts and 3D scenes' and 'achieving near-perfect retrieval accuracy', but the best reported R@1 is only 37.8% (Table 1, ScanRefer), far from near-perfect, and the paper later concedes 'the performance of the methods is relatively low' in the limitations. This grossly overstates the actual results.

The paper cites '[60] Zhang, L., Wang, M., & Liu, Q. (2022). Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval. In Proceedings of ICLR 2022.' as providing the theoretical foundation for the density correction method. No such paper appears in the ICLR 2022 proceedings, and the reference is almost certainly fabricated.

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation (4) and associated text in Section 3.2.2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The method claims to model response features with a 'minimum enclosing hypersphere' and uses the condition u_i^j o_i^T ≤ R_i, which is a linear (half-space) constraint, not a sphere. The subsequent steps that rely on a hypersphere boundary and center are therefore logically inconsistent with the stated formulation.
